features.oam: hardware IEEE 802.1ag CFM, 802.3ah EFM, Y.1731 SLM/DMM, Y.1564 and RFC 2544 test head, MEF 46/48/49
features.resiliency: sub-50 ms RSVP-TE FRR, secondary LSP, G.8031 1:1, G.8032, dual-homed VPLS/H-VPLS, BFD
features.routing-protocols: IS-IS, OSPF, BGP, RSVP-TE, LDP, Segment Routing, xSTP, G.8032, LACP, MC-LAG
features.services: MPLS L2VPN (VPLS, H-VPLS, VPWS), MPLS L3VPN (BGP), 802.1Q, 802.1ad Q-in-Q
features.timing: SyncE, IEEE 1588v2 PTP, BITS, 1PPS and ToD (DS-v14)

management.local: CLI console and out-of-band Ethernet on RJ45
management.mgmt-protocols: Console, Telnet, SSHv2, RADIUS, TACACS+, SNMP v1/2/3, xFTP, NTP, DNS resolver, NETCONF

performance.port-options: 40x SFP+; 40x SFP+ + 4x QSFP28; or 88x SFP+ (with the 48-port module)
performance.switching-capacity: 1.2 Tbps full duplex, wire speed, non-blocking

physical.overall-mm: 482 x 88.9 x 350 with rack ears (the data sheet's 133.35 height is a 3RU slip)

platform.oam-module: TM810x-OAM, full-FPGA expansion module for hardware OAM (location not documented)

power.power-envelope-note: data sheet "Max power consumption 400W", no configuration or ambient stated

gaps.note: telco.com publishes data sheets only; its support page says hardware documentation is on a support portal behind a login, whose contact is on telco.com/support. The one public Telco Systems installation guide (T-Marc 3306, MN100280) is for another product. Searched: the telco.com media library (120 PDFs), every product and knowledge-centre page, and the Wayback index of telco.com PDFs.
gaps.wanted: the TM-8104 / T-Metro 8104 hardware installation guide, from the BATM support portal.

gaps.note: Block origins are the stencil's. The two vendor fronts disagree with it differently: the yaw-corrected 2021 TM-8104 render within -3.0 to +0.4 mm with no pattern, the near-square 2022 TM-8106 front (1.8 px/mm) placing its outer SFP+ blocks about 2.2 mm further out on each side. Neither resolves better than 2-3 mm, so the stencil stands.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing, or a square-on photograph at 4 px/mm or better.

gaps.note: No image held shows the rear. The data sheets say the fans are hot-swappable and order them as TM810x-FAN, and NetBox lists four fan bays, so the rear almost certainly holds them; where, and whether it carries a ground point or anything else, is not known.
gaps.wanted: a square-on photograph of the rear, or the installation guide's rear view.

gaps.note: No data sheet states the airflow direction. NetBox gives front-to-rear, which is a community reading with no cited source, so chassis.airflow is left unset.
The TM810x-OAM "Full FPGA Expansion Module for Base System" (ordering tables, 2025) and NetBox's "OAM Expansion Bay" have no visible opening on the front; it is presumably internal. Not drawn.
gaps.wanted: the installation guide, or a photograph of the chassis with its lid off.

gaps.note: The 2025 data sheet's ordering table describes TM8104-BASE-2XX as "40x1/10GE SFP+ ports, 48x1/10GE SFP+ Line Card" and TM8104-88S-Y-2XX and TM8104-4QS-Y-2XX with the same "4x40/100GE QSFP28 Line Card" text, while the 2021 editions order the base as 40 x SFP+ with the modules separate. The configurations follow the 2021 reading and the SKU names (88S = the 48-port module, 4QS = the QSFP28 module); no part number is attached to a configuration while the table contradicts itself.
gaps.wanted: a current price list or ordering guide.

gaps.note: DS-v14 lists BITS, frequency, 1PPS and ToD in or out, and the face labels GPS, BITS 1 and 2, and ToD / E1-T1; which signal each connector carries, and in which direction, is not tabled anywhere held.
No edition gives the supplies' own rating or model number; only the chassis' 400 W maximum. Searched every data sheet held for "W", "PSU", "power supply" and "Power".
gaps.wanted: the supply's label or the installation guide's power section.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

which optics actually run in each pluggable cage - as prose in `attrs.optics-<media>` for now, which at least reaches the group, and structurally once enough vendors are in to say what the vocabulary has to hold

chassis.note: 2RU x 436.9 x 88.5 x 350 deep. The depth is the data sheet's (13.7 in, 350 mm). The face is the stencil's: its body between the ear folds is 165.1 units = 436.8 mm and its height 33.5 units = 88.6 mm at the stencil's 1:10, and its outline with ears is 482.9 mm - the 19-inch face, which is what fixes the scale. Two readings off the vendor's renders corroborate it: the 2021 render (8104-02.png, 3622 px) gives a body of 439.5 and a face of 87.8 mm, and the 2022 TM-8106 front (8106.jpg) a face aspect of 4.955, i.e. 88.8 on a 440 body. The render is yawed a little (its SFP pitch slides 14.60 -> 14.41 -> 14.34 left to right), which is why its 439.5 is not preferred over the stencil. Recorded as estimated because a stencil is a diagram symbol and no mechanical drawing is held.

chassis-height-in-the-data-sheet.note: Every data-sheet edition prints "2RU H x 19'W x 13.7'D (133.35 x 482 x 350mm)". 133.35 mm is exactly THREE rack units (3 x 44.45); 2RU is 88.9. The stencil (88.6), the 2021 render (87.8), the TM-8106 front (88.8) and NetBox (u_height 2.0) all say 2RU, so the millimetre figure is a transcription slip and 88.5 is drawn. The 482 is the 19-inch face with its ears, not the body.

ears.note: Not drawn. The stencil's ear folds are at 8.8 and 173.9 units, 23.3 mm of ear either side of the body. The data sheets order the brackets separately (TM810x-BRKT-19IN or -23IN, "Ear Side TM810x Rack Mount Brackets").

exp-slot.note: One full-width expansion slot, printed as slot 2 ("1/2/x" on the 48-port module, 1/2/1 ... 1/5/1 on the QSFP28 module). The data sheets list the two modules it takes, TM810x-48SFP+ and TM810x-4QSFP28; its size is the stencil's empty slot.

fans.note: Data sheets: "Fan: Load sharing, speed controlled, hot-swappable", orderable as TM810x-FAN. NetBox lists four fan bays. Nothing held shows where they are, so no fan is drawn (see the rear-and-fans gap).

front-layout.note: Every feature is placed from the stencil master's own vector paths, extracted to chassis millimetres (x = (unit - 8.8) x 2.6458), and then checked against the 2021 render at matched scale: PSU column x 4.9-57.9, expansion slot [59.0, 3.35] 376.7 x 33.9, vent strip y 41.2-48.4, base SFP+ blocks of 4, 8 and 8 columns, the ToD/E1-T1 and CLI/OOB stacks, four lamps. Every feature is present in both and in the same order. POSITIONS AGREE TO ABOUT 2.5 MM AND NO BETTER, and that is the render's limit, not the stencil's error: the render is yawed (its lamp pitch slides 14.60 -> 14.41 -> 14.34 across three identical blocks), and after integrating a local scale fitted to that slide its features sit within -3.0 (ToD shell) to +0.4 (base block B) of the stencil with no consistent pattern, and its body comes out 434.6 against 436.85. The in-block pitch, which both sources resolve well, agrees to 0.05 mm. See the block-spacing gap.

jack-lamps.note: L76 STANDS IN THE BASELINE ON PURPOSE, not waived (the waiver cap is for rules with no device-level fix). the console and timing jacks here ARE lamped, so the lamped part is the right one. At 4x on the 2021 render (telco.com 2021/01/8104-02.png, 5.9 px/mm) both RJ45 stacks - ToD over E1/T1 and CLI over OOB - show a bright lamp window in each outer corner of each jack, the top corners of the upper jack and the bottom corners of the lower, set in the jack housing rather than beside it; the stencil draws the same four green windows on every jack. docs/rj45-family-design.md's rule is that a console or timing jack carries no lamps, which is true of most boxes and not of this one. Revisit if a closer photograph shows the ToD or CLI windows are blanks.

jack-orientation.note: Both RJ45 stacks put their lamp windows on the OUTER corners - the top corners of the upper jack and the bottom corners of the lower - in the stencil and in the 2021 render's highlights. common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 draws its lamps on the keyway side and is keyway-down unrotated, so the upper jack is turned 180 and the lower is not.

lamps.note: One up and one down arrow lamp per column in the pale strip between the rows (common/led-arrow@1), as the render and stencil both draw. PWR, CPU1, CPU2 and FAN beside the CLI/OOB stack and SYNC beside GPS are common/led-dot@1 on the stencil's 2.6 mm and 2.1 mm lamps - the nearest library part, 2.0 mm, is used at the measured centres rather than a 4 mm lamp at a wrong pitch. The stencil colours FAN red and the rest green; no document says what any lamp's states mean.

logos.note: TWO PRINTINGS, AND THE CURRENT ONE IS DRAWN. The 2025 render (telco.com 2025/08/8104@2x.png) prints a plain TELCO SYSTEMS wordmark over T-METRO 8104 at the base board's left, as every TM-8106 image does; both are text and both are drawn. The 2021 render and the 2024 stencil print the older Telco Systems mark there instead - a red swirl beside the wordmark over "A BATM Company" - which, being a logo, would be reserved rather than drawn. No configuration can say which unit wears which, so the older printing is recorded here and not modelled.

model.note: TM-8104 data sheet (telco.com 2025/12), "TM-8104 Modular 1.2Tb Multi-Service Aggregation Platform"; earlier editions (DS-v14, 2021-03; 2021-04-20) call it the T-Metro 8104, which is what the faceplate prints.

port-numbering.note: Legends read off the 2021 render and the stencil, which agree: each column prints "1▲▼2" under the block, the upper port's number with an up arrow and the lower's with a down arrow, 1-40 left to right; "1/1/x" at the foot of the first block says these are slot 1. NetBox names them 1/1/1 to 1/1/40.

ports.note: std/sfp-ganged@1 centred on each stencil cage opening (13.91 x 9.68): upper row y 55.58, lower 71.45, columns at x 107.1 ... 149.92 (4), 166.96 ... 267.39 (8) and 284.38 ... 384.81 (8), a 14.26-14.36 pitch. The stencil's pitch agrees with the 2021 render's two undistorted blocks (14.34, 14.41) and not with the registry's touching 14.25, so these cages stand a tenth of a millimetre apart. Odd ports above, even below; the lower row is turned 180 so both rows' lips face the lamp strip.

power.note: "Max power consumption: 400W", unqualified by configuration or ambient in all five editions - filed as the chassis maximum. No supply rating and no per-module figure is published anywhere held.

psu-bays.note: Two bays at the stencil's supply faces, 50.91 x 39.43 at y 3.9 and 45.4, labelled PS1 and PS2 reading bottom to top beside them. The data sheets: "Dual redundant, hot-swappable AC or DC 24/-48VDC".

shells.note: The silver shell around each RJ45 stack and the metal frame of each SFP+ block are panel decor at the stencil's outlines (17.14 x 26.98 and 58.16 / 115.73 x 27.0); the 2021 render shows both as bright metal against the black panel.

sources.note: Five data-sheet editions (2021-03 v14, 2021-04-20, 2021-05 V2, 2021-08, 2025-12), the NetZoom stencil Telco-TM810x-04-30-2024.VSS (masters TM8104 (CF), TM810x-48SFP+, TM810x-4QSFP28), 23 vendor renders from the telco.com media library, and the NetBox devicetype-library entry Telco Systems/T-Metro-8104.yaml as a second reading. NO INSTALLATION GUIDE IS PUBLIC - telco.com routes hardware manuals to a support portal behind a login (see the install-guide gap).

timing.note: DS-v14 and V2 list the external timing interfaces: BITS in or out (1.544 Mb/s, 2.048 MHz, 2 Mb/s), frequency in or out (1.544 MHz, 2.048 MHz, 10 MHz), 1PPS and ToD in or out (NMEA 0183), SyncE and IEEE 1588v2 PTP. The face labels a GPS SMA, two BITS SMAs numbered 1 and 2, and an RJ45 stack "ToD ▲▼ E1/T1"; which signal each SMA carries beyond its label is not documented (see the timing-port-mapping gap). The BITS pair sits 8.7 mm apart, too close for common/sma-jack@1's 9.5 mm jam nut, so the bare std/sma@1 is placed.

vent.note: The perforated strip between the slot and the base board, y 41.2-48.4 across x 70.3-425.1 between the two chassis screws, from the stencil; the 2021 render shows it as two staggered rows of hexagonal holes. Hole pitch and cavity depth are not measured.
